dedupe_keys.name: noaa space weather prediction center products and data services

description: The Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) of the US National Weather Service is the official US source of space weather alerts, watches, warnings and forecasts. Its products and data pages list the NOAA space weather scales, 3-day geomagnetic forecasts, the report and forecast of solar and geophysical activity, 45-day Ap and F10.7 flux forecasts, weekly highlights and 27-day outlooks, the 30-minute aurora forecast, the relativistic electron forecast model, WSA-Enlil solar wind predictions and GOES solar and particle observations. Machine-readable products are served free of charge from the services.swpc.noaa.gov directory in JSON, text and image form, and alerts can be received by free email subscription; the SWPC also explains impacts on electric power transmission, where geomagnetically induced currents flow through power lines and transformers, and on GPS, satellites and aviation. As US government data they are public domain. Caveats: the service is organised around current operations, so long historical archives sit at NCEI and other archives, product formats change with notice, and the directory offers no search. Uses include real-time feeds for digital twins and emergency response in power grids, satellite and GNSS operations, and hazard exposure studies of geomagnetic storms; related records are the GFZ Kp index, INTERMAGNET and DONKI in this catalogue.
